A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same R2E research work. Their main text, figures, tables, equations and complete appendices are readable and support comparison, including matching relocated material.

before.justification: v2 reports original gene-ranking experiments, clinical-trial predictions, architecture ablations and evidence-annotation evaluations.

after.justification: v3 retains original empirical evaluations and adds GPT-4 baseline results, inference profiling and expanded clinical analyses.

M1.justification: Section 3.4 changes the stated negative-sampling rule from uniform sampling over all answers to excluding the true answer. The architecture, losses, retrieval, Shapley computation and auditing procedure remain intact. Appendix F retains unrestricted sampling assumptions, so whether the implementation changed is unresolved.

E1.justification: Both versions use the same biomedical literature, Gene Description Facts, Clinical Trial Outcomes, genetics evidence and annotation tasks. Held-out Biomedical Literature moves into v3 Appendix J. New comparator and threshold evaluations do not introduce distinct dataset or task coverage.

E2.justification: v3 adds a few-shot, retrieval-augmented, chain-of-thought GPT-4 prediction baseline for Clinical Trial Outcomes; GPT-4 previously served as an annotator and auditor. Table S6 also adds MCS and MLM to the corresponding validation-set ablation comparison, alongside the retained Hadamard and PubMedBERT variants.

E3.justification: v3 introduces GPT-4 prediction evaluation using three confidence cutoffs and clinical relative-success comparisons across thresholds and matched positive-prediction counts. It removes the temporal-training experimental protocols. The genetic-insight subset is reported as 4,056 rather than 4,226 hypotheses without explaining the revision; this does not establish that experiments were rerun.

E4.justification: v3 expands component ablations in Table S6, adds prediction/explanation profiling and relative-success threshold curves, and extends disease-area analysis to audited predictions. Conversely, v2's temporal-training analyses on held-out literature and clinical outcomes, including Tables S7 and S8, are removed. Existing annotation and auditing case studies remain.

E5.justification: v2 already reports confidence intervals and a DeLong test. v3 explicitly identifies Katz confidence intervals, introduces Z-tests for relative-success comparisons and broadens significance reporting. Neither version establishes repeated model-training runs or seed-based uncertainty estimates.

E6.justification: Most main benchmark scores remain unchanged, but v3 adds substantial results: GPT-4 relative success of 1.77 versus 2.05 for combined-evidence R2E-cor at 609 positive predictions, additional ablation scores and runtime measurements. Disease-area curves also change, with genetics-only R2E falling below AUROC 0.5 for dermatological and anti-infective diseases. Temporal-training results are removed.

T1.justification: Section 3.4 revises the formal support of negative sampling by excluding the true answer, while Appendix F retains independence and 1/|A| assumptions without reconciliation. The Shapley and frequency-correction derivations otherwise remain unchanged. The new relative-success equation merely states the formula for a metric already used in v2.

C1.justification: The central explainability, evidence updating, multimodality and benchmark contributions are retained. v3 adds the main claim of outperforming the GPT-4 prediction baseline and qualifies the broad baseline-superiority conclusion as matching or outperforming literature-based models. The new contribution list largely consolidates existing claims.

C2.justification: v3 adds explanations linking gene-description performance to established knowledge, rare-gene performance to retrieval access, and limited multimodal gains to evidence imbalance and redundancy. Appendix V adds GPT-4 applicability, cost and temporal-contamination qualifications. Existing soft-semantic matching interpretations and clinical-label limitations remain.

D1.justification: New Appendix H documents exact FAISS IndexFlatIP searches, approximately 300 GB index memory and CPU profiling configurations. Appendix V supplies the new GPT-4 baseline's full prompt and decision cutoffs. Existing R2E hyperparameters, training hardware, dataset access and restrictions on releasing code and weights remain substantially unchanged.

R1.justification: v3 refines positioning against training-data attribution and generative LLMs, adding Hammoudeh and Lowd, Sui, Lee, Mountjoy and Katz citations while removing Pandl and Yogatama. The central retrieval/explainability positioning remains. Minikel's 2023-to-2024 reference change identifies the same work's publication update, not a new comparator.

P1.justification: The abstract and introduction are substantially rewritten, explicit contribution bullets are added, and methods and results are reorganized. Held-out literature evaluation moves to an appendix, Discussion becomes a shorter Conclusions section, and the clinical appendix gains thematic subsections. These are extensive narrative changes beyond the added experiments.

P2.justification: v3 redraws the overview and architecture schematics, adds the relative-success figure, and redesigns disease-area and similarity plots. It expands ablation and clinical tables, relocates the held-out literature table, and removes temporal-training tables. Appendix plots previously occupying separate pages are integrated with explanatory text.

improvement.justification: The documented GPT-4 comparison, threshold analyses and resource profiling make R2E's comparative and practical value easier to assess, while the reorganization improves clarity. The net gain is limited by removal of temporal-training evidence and unresolved reporting issues, particularly the unexplained genetic-insight sample-count revision and disagreement between the negative-sampling description and Appendix F.
